analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation: docs/reference/protocol-messages.md head lines 202-219 add a "Close codes and the reconnect wait" section. No code, wire frames, keys, authorization logic, or storage behavior change. I read both units in full.

The new text says the provider reads only the WebSocket close code (1012 versus anything else) and ignores the close reason. It says 1012 selects a delay drawn from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff. It says a session open for stableSessionDuration or longer, counted from its register frame, resets the backoff, and that every reconnect sends a fresh register.

Threat-model fit: TB-002 treats the coordinator as trusted, so a coordinator-sent 1012 only paces reconnects. A coordinator that is impersonated or compromised could hold providers off, but that is existing exposure and not new here. The doc says the backoff does not grow on 1012, so a coordinator or on-path attacker that repeatedly sends 1012 could keep reconnect delay at the restart range. This affects availability only and cannot grant trust.

The doc states that every reconnect sends a fresh register. That is consistent with the TB-011 and T-053 binding of a fresh socket nonce to one registered socket, so no endpoint-resumption or App Attest authorization invariant is weakened.

Remaining integration question: I could not verify the behavior of CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, serviceRestartDelayRange, or stableSessionDuration, because that source was not supplied. The claims are unverified against code. The sections of the file that were not changed (app attest resume, drain, busy fields) are pre-existing and were not re-evaluated as new.
